concept: Magnetic flux Φ = BA cos θ
prompt: A coil of area $0.020\ \text{m}^{2}$ is in a uniform 0.30 T field. The normal to the coil makes $60^{\circ}$ with the field. Calculate the flux through the coil, and state the angle for maximum flux.
markscheme: $\Phi=BA\cos\theta=0.30\times0.020\times\cos60^{\circ}=3.0\times10^{-3}$ Wb **(A1)**; maximum when the normal is parallel to the field ($\theta=0$, plane of coil perpendicular to $B$) **(A1)**

prompt: The flux through each turn of a 200-turn coil falls uniformly from $3.0\times10^{-3}$ Wb to zero in 0.15 s. Calculate the magnitude of the induced emf.

An aircraft with a 30 m wingspan flies horizontally at $250\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ where the vertical component of the Earth's magnetic field is $4.0\times10^{-5}$ T. Calculate the emf induced between the wing tips, and explain why it cannot drive a current through a wire connected across the wings.
markscheme: $\varepsilon=BvL=4.0\times10^{-5}\times250\times30=0.30$ V **(A1)**; the connecting wire moves through the same field and has the same emf induced in it, cancelling around the circuit **(R1)**

prompt:
The north pole of a bar magnet is pushed into a coil connected to a meter.

**(a)** State the polarity of the end of the coil facing the magnet. **[1]**

**(b)** Explain how this is a consequence of conservation of energy. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** North — the induced current opposes the change producing it, so it repels the approaching N pole **(A1)**

**(b)** Work must be done against this repulsion to push the magnet in **(R1)**; that work is the source of the electrical energy in the circuit — if the induced pole attracted, energy would be created from nothing **(R1)**

concept: Sinusoidal emf from a rotating coil
prompt:
A coil of 100 turns and area $0.010\ \text{m}^{2}$ rotates at 50 Hz in a uniform 0.20 T field.

**(a)** Calculate the peak emf. **[2]**

**(b)** State the orientation of the coil when the emf is maximum. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\varepsilon_0=BAN\omega=0.20\times0.010\times100\times2\pi\times50$ **(M1)** $=63$ V **(A1)**

**(b)** When the plane of the coil is parallel to the field (flux zero, but changing fastest) **(A1)**

prompt: The rotation frequency of a generator coil is doubled. What happens to the peak emf and the frequency of the output?
markscheme: **D.** $\varepsilon_0=BAN\omega$, so doubling $\omega$ doubles the peak emf, and the output alternates twice as often.
